title: Formal laws for the categorical trace
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and coefficient conventions [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Use the categorical trace of [def-trf-categorical-trace] on perfect ordinary module complexes [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and its same signed dual-frame construction over any commutative coefficient ring. In this proposition $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ means $\operatorname{Perf}(A)$, as in that trace definition; it does not mean all complexes with finite cohomology. For a field $F$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(F)=D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(F)$ has bounded finite-dimensional cohomology [def-weil-point-fd-complexes]. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, in the common-stage notation [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]: compute the endomorphism, cohomology and scalar trace at a common finite coefficient-field stage and extend scalars to $\Qlb$.

1. Conjugacy invariance. For perfect $P_1,P_2$ and endomorphisms $v_i$ in $D(A)$, if $w:P_1\xrightarrow{\sim}P_2$ satisfies $v_2\circ w=w\circ v_1$, then $\operatorname{tr}_A(v_1\mid P_1)=\operatorname{tr}_A(v_2\mid P_2)$.
2. Filtered additivity. Suppose $P'\to P\to P''\to P'[1]$ is a distinguished triangle of perfect complexes and $(v',v,v'')$ has filtered origin: the triangle and these endomorphisms are induced by a pair of complexes $K'\subset K$ and an endomorphism in the category obtained by inverting filtration-preserving quasi-isomorphisms on both $K'$ and $K/K'$ in the filtered homotopy category. Then $\operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P)=\operatorname{tr}_A(v'\mid P')+\operatorname{tr}_A(v''\mid P'')$. In particular this applies to a filtration-preserving chain endomorphism of a short exact sequence of bounded finite-projective complexes. The corresponding assertion for arbitrary endomorphisms of Verdier distinguished triangles is false: over $R=\mathbf Z/4$, the triangle from $0\to R[-1]\to[R\xrightarrow{2}R]\to R\to0$, with middle endomorphism $(0,2)$ in degrees $0,1$ and zero endomorphisms on the ends, has middle trace $-2\neq0$ (Stacks Tag 087J).
3. Scalar extension. For any ring homomorphism $\rho:A\to B$ of commutative rings, any perfect $P$ and its endomorphism $v$, the extended complex is perfect and $\rho(\operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P))=\operatorname{tr}_B(v\otimes_A^LB\mid P\otimes_A^LB)$, where $-\otimes_A^LB:D(A)\to D(B)$ is the total left derived functor [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of termwise extension of scalars along $\rho$ [def-weil-module-base-change].
4. Supertrace over a field. For $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, $P\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Lambda)$ and $v:P\to P$, $\operatorname{tr}_\Lambda(v\mid P)=\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(H^i(v)\mid H^i(P))$.

proof.text: Choose bounded finite-projective representatives for the perfect complexes, using [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. By [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], each derived morphism between them has a chain representative, and equal derived morphisms give homotopic representatives. Use the explicit signed dual-frame evaluation and coevaluation of [def-trf-categorical-trace]; [lem-trf-chain-supertrace] identifies their trace with $\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(v^i)$ and makes it independent of homotopies and representatives. These are ordinary module complexes, not pro-etale sheaf complexes.

For clause (1), use the canonical Koszul braiding and the canonical right duals supplied by def-trf-categorical-trace for the two perfect objects. Unfold the finite-coefficient specialization and perfectCategoricalTrace. The existing source-library theorem CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.trace_eq_of_iso applies to w and the symmetry of the given intertwining equation. Its proof transports the right-dual pairing, uses cyclicity of the coevaluation--braiding--evaluation composite, and cancels w.hom and w.inv. Apply the same perfectTraceScalar function to the resulting equality of endomorphisms of the tensor unit. No chain model or supertrace assertion is needed for this clause.

source.place: Clause (1), the two duality squares and trace-composite calculation

proof.text: For clause (2), the filtered-origin hypothesis gives an object and endomorphism to which [lem-trf-filtered-projective-model] applies: its graded pieces are precisely the perfect $P'$ and $P''$. Obtain $M'\subset M$ with quotient $M''$ and a filtration-preserving chain endomorphism. Split $M^i=M'^i\oplus M''^i$ degreewise; its component has blocks $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\beta^i&s^i\\0&\alpha^i\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Using dual frames on the two summands, the frame expression for its trace is the sum of the diagonal frame expressions: the dual functionals from the second summand vanish on the off-diagonal image in the first. Thus $\operatorname{Tr}(\bar v^i)=\operatorname{Tr}(\beta^i)+\operatorname{Tr}(\alpha^i)$. Multiply by $(-1)^i$, sum over the finite degree range, and apply [lem-trf-chain-supertrace] on each of the three complexes. This gives the required additivity, with clause (1) identifying the chosen models with the given objects.

source.place: Clause (2), filtered model and block-triangular calculation; Stacks Tag 03TJ

proof.text: The warning in (2) is verified directly. The degreewise split sequence gives a distinguished triangle: the cone-to-quotient map has contractible kernel, by the explicit calculation in step 7 and the cone definition [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $R=\mathbf Z/4$ and $M=[R\xrightarrow{2}R]$ in degrees $0,1$, $v=(0,2)$ is a chain map because $2\cdot2=0$. For the inclusion $i:R[-1]\to M$, the map $vi$ is null-homotopic via $h^1=1:R\to M^0=R$; the projection $p:M\to R[0]$ satisfies $pv=0$ strictly. The last triangle square has zero maps on both sides. Hence $(0,v,0)$ is an endomorphism of this distinguished triangle, while [lem-trf-chain-supertrace] gives middle trace $0-2=-2\neq0$ and both end traces zero. Its restriction to the subcomplex is $2$, not the prescribed zero; it is therefore not this triple's filtered lift.

For clause (3), write $P=Q(M)$ with $M$ bounded finite projective. Projective terms are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], so [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $M$ K-flat; consequently the counit of the derived functor at $M$ is an isomorphism by [lem-pc-kflat-scalar-extension-counit], so $Q(M\otimes_A B)$ computes $P\otimes_A^L B$ without assuming $B$ flat, and by naturality of the counit the chain map $v\otimes1$ represents $v\otimes_A^LB$. Tensor a finite splitting $M^i\xrightarrow{\iota}A^N\xrightarrow{\pi}M^i$ with $B$: the equation $\pi\iota=1$ remains true, so the extended terms are finite projective. If $(e_a,\epsilon_a)$ is its dual frame, then $(e_a\otimes1,\epsilon_{a,B})$ is the extended frame with $\epsilon_{a,B}(x\otimes b)=\rho(\epsilon_a(x))b$. Hence $\operatorname{Tr}_B(v^i\otimes1)=\sum_a\rho(\epsilon_a(v^ie_a))=\rho(\operatorname{Tr}_A(v^i))$. Apply [lem-trf-chain-supertrace] over $A$ and over $B$ and move $\rho$ through the finite signed sum. This proves (3) and identifies exactly the defining dual-frame trace after extension.

source.place: Clause (3), scalar extension; corrected K-flat representative argument

proof.text: For clause (4) over a field $F$, first justify the bounded finite-dimensional chain model from the cohomological definition [def-weil-point-fd-complexes]. Every vector-space quotient is projective by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-projective]; lift its identity through the quotient surjection using [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], obtaining a section and hence a complement. In any representative $C$, choose such complements $Z^i=B^i\oplus H_i$ and $C^i=Z^i\oplus L^i$, where $Z^i=\ker d^i$, $B^i=\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$ and $d:L^i\cong B^{i+1}$. Inclusion of the zero-differential complex $H=(H_i)$ into $C$ is a quasi-isomorphism, since it induces $H_i\cong H^i(C)$; $H$ is bounded and finite-dimensional by the defining hypotheses. Thus $P$ is perfect. Choose a bounded finite-dimensional representative $M$ and a chain endomorphism representing $v$ by [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative].

source.place: Clause (4), justification of the bounded finite-dimensional representative

proof.text: For this bounded $M$, define $T_i^j=M^j$ for $j<i$, $T_i^i=\ker d^i$, and $T_i^j=0$ for $j>i$. These subcomplexes are stable under the chain endomorphism. The quotient $C_i=T_{i+1}/T_i$ is zero except for $M^i/\ker d^i\cong\operatorname{im}d^i$ in degree $i$ and $\ker d^{i+1}$ in degree $i+1$; its differential is inclusion. Each $0\to T_i\to T_{i+1}\to C_i\to0$ splits degreewise, by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-projective] and the identity-lifting definition [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and its induced endomorphisms have filtered origin. Its cone triangle is the given short-exact-sequence triangle: the natural map $\operatorname{Cone}(T_i\to T_{i+1})\to C_i$ has kernel the cone of $1_{T_i}$, with terms $T_i^n\oplus T_i^{n+1}$ and differential $(x,y)\mapsto(d x+y,-d y)$. The degree-minus-one map $h(x,y)=(0,x)$ satisfies $dh+hd=1$, so this kernel is acyclic. The cone-to-quotient map is a quasi-isomorphism: to lift a quotient cycle, lift it arbitrarily and subtract a kernel element whose differential is the resulting kernel-valued defect; a lifted cycle mapping to a quotient boundary is itself a boundary after the same correction in the acyclic kernel. This verifies the distinguished-triangle hypothesis in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Clause (4), canonical truncations and explicit two-term quotient

proof.text: Apply the already proved filtered-additivity calculation of step 3 over $F$ (the calculation used only a commutative ring) to $T_i\subset T_{i+1}$. On $C_i$, [lem-trf-chain-supertrace] gives $(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(v|\operatorname{im}d^i)+(-1)^{i+1}\operatorname{Tr}(v|\ker d^{i+1})$. Using [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-projective] and [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] to lift the identity of the quotient, split $0\to\operatorname{im}d^i\to\ker d^{i+1}\to H^{i+1}(M)\to0$; the endomorphism is block triangular and its diagonal trace is the sum of the subspace and quotient traces. The displayed increment is therefore $(-1)^{i+1}\operatorname{Tr}(H^{i+1}(v))$. If $M$ is supported in $[a,b]$, then $T_{a-1}=0$ and $T_b=M$. Summing the increments for $i=a-1,\ldots,b-1$ telescopes and proves (4) over $E$, and over any field.

source.place: Clause (4), increment calculation and finite induction

proof.text: For the common-stage interpretation at $\Qlb$, [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category] represents $P$ at a finite field $E_0$ and $v$ at some finite common extension $L$. Apply the preceding field calculation at $L$ and embed the resulting scalar in $\Qlb$. On extending $L$ further, [def-weil-finite-dimensional-complex-scalar-extension] identifies cohomology with its scalar extension; the dual-frame calculation of step 5 shows that the trace on both the complex and each cohomology space extends by the same field inclusion. Thus both sides are independent of the common stage. The same formula holds in the actual ordinary-module category $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$ directly by steps 6--8; no equivalence of these two categories is assumed.

proof_origin.place: Original clauses (2)--(4) retained as plans; clause (1) implemented using WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Rigid.Braided.trace_eq_of_iso, which proves the same categorical duality cancellation.
